en: Mount Pinatubo's massive 1991 eruption cooled the global average temperature by about half a degree Celsius for several years.
Olympus Mons on Mars is the tallest known volcano in our solar system, standing nearly three times higher than Mount Everest.
Sirius, also known as the Dog Star, is the brightest star visible in Earth's night sky from the Northern Hemisphere.
The Apollo 11 astronauts landed on the Moon's Sea of Tranquility, a large, dark basaltic plain formed by ancient volcanic eruptions.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan flows directly into the sea, making its lower half subject to tidal influences.
Super Typhoon Yolanda, known internationally as Haiyan, produced some of the highest wind speeds ever recorded on land when it struck the Philippines.
Talc is officially rated as number one on the Mohs hardness scale, making it the softest known natural mineral on Earth.
The rich volcanic soil around Taal Volcano helps local farmers in Batangas grow abundant crops like coffee and pineapple.
Baguio City experiences a subtropical highland climate, giving it significantly cooler average temperatures than the rest of the lowland Philippines.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao are carved into steep mountain slopes, demonstrating how farmers utilize thin, rocky soil.
Jupiter's moon Europa has a smooth, icy surface that scientists believe hides a massive, liquid saltwater ocean beneath its frozen crust.
Mount Mayon in Albay is famous for its perfect cone shape, which is built up by layers of hardened lava and ash.
